finshotsAward.title: Google Play Best App 2020
finshotsAward.story: Dev designed the Finshots mobile app end-to-end, turning newsletter readers into daily app users with a centralized hub for financial news.
finshotsAward.detail: The app hit **100k+ downloads**, earned a **4.9★** Play Store rating, and was named **Google Play's Best App of 2020**, the project that launched Dev's product design career.

philosophy.userCenteredDesc: I design with care, always keeping **the user at the center of every decision.**
philosophy.humanTechDesc: Technology should feel natural and intuitive, **built for humans.**
philosophy.iterativeDesc: Great design is born from **continuous refinement and learning from feedback.**
philosophy.accessibilityDesc: Designing inclusively ensures **everyone can access and enjoy digital experiences.**

luxbrew.question: Two product storytelling studies around a premium coffee machine: the slow reveal, then the lightweight setup flow.

perplexity.title: Perplexity studies
perplexity.question: Two recreation studies exploring how Perplexity turns empty states and upgrade moments into calmer invitations.

botOrb.title: Bot orb
botOrb.question: A face for the agent — gaze, blink, and presence on a phone screen.
botOrb.notes: The same orb that answers questions elsewhere on this site, given a body and a phone to live on. Its gaze drifts on its own timer, it blinks at uneven intervals, and the surface underneath keeps moving — three loops that never quite line up, which is what stops it reading as a loading spinner. The whole thing is CSS and transforms, no canvas, so it costs almost nothing to keep on screen.
botOrb.accessibilityLabel: Interactive bot orb on a phone screen

dewAi.title: Dew AI
dewAi.question: An interactive AI character — a face for conversation, built with Whisper from ChatGPT, SwiftUI, Rive, and Xcode.
dewAi.notes: A character you talk to rather than type at. Whisper handles the listening, Rive carries the face, and SwiftUI holds the two together — so speech drives expression directly instead of turning into a transcript first. Most of the work went into the pauses: what the face does while it waits, and how it hands the turn back.

coachingThread.title: Coaching in a thread
coachingThread.question: Can an entire training plan live inside one conversation?
coachingThread.notes: A training plan with no dashboard, no charts, no weekly summary screen — just a thread. The Claude API does the programming, and the interface question is what stays: how a plan holds its shape when every change arrives as a message, and how much structure a conversation can carry before it needs a screen of its own.

albumArt.title: Audio-reactive album art
albumArt.question: What if cover art moved to the waveform? A Spotify study.
albumArt.notes: Cover art that answers the waveform. Metal shaders sample the track and push the artwork around in time with it, so the sleeve behaves less like a thumbnail and more like the room the song is playing in. A recreation study, built to find out how far a familiar surface can move before it stops feeling like Spotify.
albumArt.accessibilityLabel: Audio-reactive album artwork glitching to music, Spotify study

monthsDial.title: Koi pond
monthsDial.question: What if a calm pond invited your finger to stir the water?
monthsDial.notes: A pond that reacts to being touched. Drag across the water and the ripples spread, the lilies drift, and the fish scatter and regroup — no controls, no target, nothing to complete. It started as a month picker and turned into a study of gesture feedback with no task attached to it.
monthsDial.accessibilityLabel: Interactive koi pond with lily pads, flowers, and ripples responding to touch

luxbrewReveal.title: LuxBrew — the reveal
luxbrewReveal.question: How slowly can a product page move and still feel premium?
luxbrewReveal.notes: A product page that refuses to hurry. The machine assembles as you scroll, one part at a time, and the copy waits for it — the question being how slow a reveal can get before patience turns into impatience. 3D and art direction doing the selling, with the layout staying out of the way.
luxbrewReveal.accessibilityLabel: LuxBrew coffee machine product page, hand reaching for the cup

perplexityHome.title: Where knowledge begins
perplexityHome.question: What makes Perplexity's blank state feel like an invitation?
perplexityHome.notes: A recreation of Perplexity's home screen, built to work out why an empty state can feel like an invitation instead of a void. Line-art animation gives the blank page something to do while it waits, and the cursor gets somewhere to look before there is anything to read.
perplexityHome.accessibilityLabel: Perplexity home screen recreation with line-art animation

gentlePaywall.title: The gentle paywall
gentlePaywall.question: Can an upgrade screen persuade without pressuring?
gentlePaywall.notes: The upgrade moment, recreated as something other than a wall. Illustration carries the ask, the tone stays level, and the exit stays obvious — a study of how much of a paywall's reputation comes from its manners rather than its price.

luxbrewSetup.title: LuxBrew — guided setup
luxbrewSetup.question: How little UI does hardware onboarding actually need?
luxbrewSetup.notes: The other half of LuxBrew: what happens after the box is open. A setup flow of few steps and fewer words, where the writing does the teaching and the illustration confirms you got it right, rather than a progress bar counting screens at you.

caseStudy.finshotsIntro1: As Finshots continued to establish itself as a trusted platform for financial news, primarily via email newsletters and the website, we noticed a significant challenge. While readers appreciated the high-quality content, navigating and revisiting older stories through emails or web searches became a cumbersome task.
caseStudy.finshotsIntro2: Feedback from social media and user surveys emphasized a growing demand for a more streamlined and engaging way to access financial insights. This created an opportunity to rethink how we delivered value to our audience and improve the accessibility of our content.
caseStudy.finshotsPossibleSolutions: After validating the problem and exploring potential solutions, we have determined that developing a mobile app is the best approach to address these challenges. The mobile app will offer a dedicated, user-friendly environment for accessing and rediscovering our financial insights on the go.
caseStudy.finshotsResultsIntro: The app received highly positive user feedback upon release. During the testing period and after launch, it became clear our reimagined interfaces and streamlined workflows better met customers' needs.
